title: The Google Play 12-tester rule is killing solo dev motivation. How are you guys actually dealing with this?
author: KeismeyStudio
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I’m just a hobbyist building small mobile browser games with AI for fun ($0 budget, 100% free, no ads). I wanted to package my games so people could play them more easily, and looked into putting them on the Google Play Store.

And then I saw it: the mandatory **12 closed testers for 14 consecutive days rule** for individual accounts. 💀

Honestly, it completely deflated my motivation. For a tiny solo web game project, having to recruit and manage an external testing squad just to get past the gatekeeper feels absurd.

I guess I'll just stick to a PWA on GitHub Pages for now (`[https://keismey.github.io/](https://keismey.github.io/)`), where players can just use it straight from their browser without store bureaucracy.

But seriously, how do solo devs actually survive or bypass this 12-tester rule without losing their sanity? Is everyone just using dedicated swap groups, or abandoning native stores entirely?

Would love to hear your experiences.

replies.author: AnAnnouncer
replies.body:
So there are two types of Google Play Developer accounts, *individual* and *organization*. Both are valid accounts with fully unlocked Google Play Developer features, but Google has been slowly limiting individual accounts in other ways, such as preventing you from releasing applications with sensitive permissions such as VPN or introducing this mandatory "closed testers" requirement. Organization accounts on the other hand don't have such limits, you don't need testers if you have an organization account.

You paid $25 to open an *Individual* account. Individual accounts are for individuals (you), organization accounts are for legal entities (LLC, LTD, Corp., etc). Even if you're the only appointed director/employee in such a legal entity. Though there's still a confusion Google isn't keen to clarify about whether a solo proprietor should have an individual or organization account.

Google Play functions with monetization in mind, and I would've recommended to ask your LLM of choice on how to set a legal entity up for a business, but for a fully free project, that'd be overkill, so Google kind of leaves you on the outskirts of its business strategy with this 12-tester requirement.

P.S. There are Reddit communities where you can ask people to be your testers in exchange for you being theirs, though the success varies greatly and they might not appreciate AI-assisted games too much.
